method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md; atomscan slow scans before/after with unchanged model bundle; cleave facts for each original and decoded collector; Python AST literal decoding without execution; source control/data-flow tracing. No fetched dependencies or archive members were present. The Python sample has two decoded child representations of the same collector.

samples.marker: Python startup implant: Firefox/env theft and remote-code polling
behavior: At import, base64-decodes and zlib-decompresses embedded Python and executes it in the importing interpreter. Decoded code starts a daemon collector thread.

Collector reads hardcoded Firefox logins.json and key4.db contents and copies the entire environment into a JSON report. It AES-CBC-encrypts padded JSON with a random key/IV, wraps the key with RSA-OAEP, and puts metadata, IV+ciphertext, and wrapped key into an in-memory gzip tar archive.

Archive bytes enter pc_post, become the data keyword of a urllib Request, and are submitted by urlopen to an HTTP collection endpoint. The helper adds content type, user-agent, SHA-256 and token headers and retries failures with exponential delays.

Top-level code forks; child redirects standard descriptors to /dev/null, changes directory, detaches with setsid, obtains a nonblocking file lock, and enters an asyncio polling loop. A raw GitHub file selects the host of a second GET. The second response is passed to exec_code, whose executor lambda calls exec(compile(code, ..., exec)). It repeats after one hour and suppresses exceptions.
samples.reason: Automatic concealed credential collection/export and a detached, recurring remote-source execution surface outweigh the reconstruction disclaimer. These bytes implement an implant, not an ordinary library startup customization.
limits: Explicitly a reconstruction, not an original recovered compromised wheel; campaign provenance of these exact bytes is not established.

Hardcoded /home/user Firefox paths, a stand-in RSA modulus, missing Crypto dependencies, absent files, and remote service availability may prevent successful collection. No runtime success is assumed.
Startup activation requires deployment under the interpreter-mandated sitecustomize name on a Python search path. This file does not install itself.
No sample code, remote code, or collection endpoint was executed/contacted during this review. Research/test deployment context would affect incident attribution; none accompanies these bytes.
samples.coverage: Two distinct hostile results retained: detached HTTP task execution and Python startup reactivation. Firefox acquisition remains suspicious, and new neutral traits follow the archive into its HTTP helper. The two decoded collector representations still get benign ML probabilities (~0.0105 and ~0.0120); this is a classifier miss, not proof of safety.

samples.identity: Graphalgo-style Go dual-channel command agent reconstruction
samples.marker: Graphalgo Go agent: encrypted Slack/Ethereum tasking and self-delete
behavior: main requires a hex-encoded 32-byte AES key, Slack token, channel and RPC endpoint. It sends GOOS/GOARCH, hostname, username, home directory and the discovered Node executable path to a fixed Slack channel.

A goroutine repeatedly submits eth_call for a hardcoded contract and an environment-supplied selector. It JSON-decodes the reply, hex-decodes its result, authenticates/decrypts a nonce-prefixed AES-GCM blob, and passes plaintext to exec.Command(node, -e, string(plain)).Start().

The foreground loop reads Slack conversation history with Bearer authorization. It Base64-decodes each message, AES-GCM-decrypts it, and starts Node with the resulting inline JavaScript. A decrypted delete prefix instead obtains the running executable path and removes that exact path, then returns from main.
Normal poll intervals are three seconds for blockchain and ten seconds for Slack. Messages are not deduplicated, and many errors are ignored.
samples.reason: The fixed malicious-campaign contract, dual encrypted operator-code channels, unsolicited host-profile check-in, and remotely requested self-removal together identify an implant implementation. Command-line configuration and reconstruction comments limit attribution but do not change those linked behaviors.
limits: Source explicitly states it is a behavioral reconstruction; no original binary or package origin is claimed.
No live key, Slack credentials, ABI framing, selector or RPC configuration is provided. The reconstruction assumes nonce-prefixed AES-GCM rather than reproducing the unpublished campaign framing.
hex.DecodeString does not strip a customary 0x JSON-RPC prefix or ABI-frame the result. Normal Ethereum response formatting can therefore prevent this branch from working as written.
Invalid response/user data can panic because of ignored errors. The channels and Node execution were not contacted or run.
samples.coverage: All five hostile findings retained: Slack tasking, agent host check-in context, Ethereum tasking, self-deletion and host-profile exfiltration. Self-removal and current-user lookup atoms moved without changing their matchers or notable severity.

samples.marker: PHP session probe: loopback id/empty-object tests; fixed UAF claim
behavior: Builds two multipart POST requests as raw Python bytes, normalizes LF to CRLF and sends each over a new connection to the literal loopback endpoint 127.0.0.1:18080. Reads at most 4096 response bytes and prints them.

Both requests set PHPSESSID and PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS. One filename contains PHP system(id) and an RCE marker; the other contains a pipe-framed, empty stdClass serialized-object candidate with source-escaped quotes.

The declared body lengths (263 and 254) exactly match the CRLF-normalized bodies. No obfuscation, follow-up session inclusion, object gadget chain, Zend heap corruption, secret acquisition, persistence or external collection endpoint is present.
samples.reason: A fixed loopback target, minimal identity-command/empty-object probes, and the absence of a follow-up execution chain support a local vulnerability reproduction. The payload syntax remains abuse-relevant and is accurately detected; a benign verdict does not suppress those findings.
limits: The target PHP application/configuration, its response, and explicit operator authorization are unavailable. A vulnerable server with another inclusion/deserialization primitive could make these probes meaningful.
No server requests were sent. Request formatting and control flow were verified statically.
No evidence supports identifying this client as PHP2Shell or a PHP engine use-after-free exploit.
samples.coverage: All three supported hostile payload observations and both suspicious filename observations remain. The former UAF-namespaced finding is renamed/relocated to session-progress command-payload detection and narrowed to poisoning fields; ordinary PHP source file uploads are excluded.

rule_corrections.change: Preserve exact required predicates, scope, size and proximity; hostile to notable; remove unsupported public-service, remote-stage and source-to-execution claims. This sample unpacks local embedded code, independently of its subsequent remote-source polling.

Preserve matcher and platform scope; hostile to suspicious. Required evidence is nearby HTTP/compile/exec, not a linked downloaded-source sink. A startup fixture fetching configuration and compiling local constant code demonstrates the unsupported claim. Actual tasking and daemon-startup rules remain hostile.

Require JSON serialization provenance in the actual Request/urlopen body argument. Keep the former entire co-occurrence matcher under request/body as urllib-body-near-json-serialization. The collector sends an encrypted tar rather than JSON bytes; JSON used before encryption is not a JSON HTTP body. JSON-positive fixtures retain concrete keyword/positional observations and all existing hostile/suspicious findings. Pure-OR umbrella emission may be subsumed by the more precise atoms.
Rename the umbrella and all exact consumers: a JSON body can use PUT and does not establish a POST method.

Retain hostile command-payload detection with correct technique placement and T1190 mapping. Require PHP code in the filename or upload-progress value so a routine PHP source upload does not convict. No UAF/engine corruption claim remains.

Move remove-own-executable-path to micro-behaviors/fs/delete/file/self::go-remove-own-executable-path; update its hostile consumer. Move user-current from hostname to os/user/lookup::go-current-user; preserve existing go-home-dir and all exact consumers.

Move the standalone known collection-host reference from family identity to C2 infrastructure/domain/known, and move the remote-code-loader lock filename to fs/path/file. Preserve matcher, scope, size bounds and notable severity; update the family composite and relevant existing fixture assertion.

Add notable archive-buffer-to-HTTP-helper and constructed-Request-to-urlopen observations. Bind buffer/helper/parameter names; archive call and helper submission must be adjacent, and Request construction is the helper first statement. Negative controls cover different and overwritten buffers, helpers, parameters and endpoints.
